To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The hippocampus operates as a pattern associating autoassociation network, which enables rapid, one-trail, associations between any place and an object or event, and which enables recall of the whole memory from any part.

the CA3 system is an autoassociative attractor network that provides for rapid one-trial associative learning, and for completion of the memory during recall from a partial cue; and that the neocortical system is a hierarchical series of pattern-associative networks that retrieve a complete pattern from any partial cue.

(a) the CA3 system operates in a single attractor mode to enable pattern completion; (b) the dentate granular cells operate in a competitive mode to enable pattern separation; (c) neocortical backprojection systems operate in a hierarchical pattern associator mode to enable recall of neocortical patterns; and (d) competitive networks perform pattern separation, clustering, and categorisation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms for pattern separation and pattern completion in the brain, and the implications for learning and memory.

the mechanisms by which the hippocampus performs pattern completion, pattern separation, and pattern generalization in the context of the theory that the hippocampal formation is an associative memory system that provides the neocortex with a complete memory of the world.

how information is stored and recalled in the hippocampus, and how this information can be retrieved in the neocortex, and the mechanisms that allow for pattern completion, pattern separation, and pattern generalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pattern separation is performed by competitive networks, pattern completion by autoassociative networks, and pattern generalization by pattern associator networks.

(i) pattern separation is performed by a number of different systems including the dentate gyrus, CA3 recurrent collateral synapses and CA3 to CA1 synapses, (ii) pattern completion is performed in the CA3 autoassociation network, (iii) pattern generalisation is performed in each of the hierarchical pattern associators implemented by the perforant path, the CA3 to CA2 synapses, the CA2 to CA1 synapse, and the CA1 to neocortex
the hippocampus performs pattern completion and pattern generalization, while the neocortex performs pattern completion and also pattern separation, clustering, and categorisation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hippocampal system is a pattern associator, and the neocortex performs pattern generalization.
the CA3 system operates in a single attractor mode to provide for pattern completion, and the dentate gyrus operates in competitive mode to perform pattern separation.

the hippocampus performs pattern completion to retrieve a whole memory from any part, and pattern separation to enable independent storage of many memories in CA3, while the neocortex performs pattern generalization and pattern completion to retrieve complete cortical representations from partial representations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pattern separation and pattern completion are complementary functions of the hippocampal formation and that pattern completion in the hippocampus enables pattern generalization in neocortical areas.
pattern separation is a fundamental mechanism in the neocortex and hippocampus that enables the formation of new memories, and that pattern completion is also fundamental to recall of those memories.
the hippocampus and cortex operate together as an associative memory system that can perform pattern completion, pattern separation, and pattern generalization.
